issues.legal_issue: A party may not be permitted to pay court fee on a counterclaim after the prescribed time has expired when the counterclaim was not taken up as an issue in the trial.
material_facts: The defendant claimed a counterclaim for improvements made to the property in the written statement.
No issue concerning the counterclaim had been framed by the trial court.
No court fee had been paid on the counterclaim within the prescribed time.
Permission to pay the fee and have an issue framed was sought only at a later stage of the proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The party could not be allowed to pay the court fee at that late stage; the counterclaim was barred by limitation.
issues.legal_principle: Where the court fee on a counterclaim is not paid within the prescribed time, the counterclaim is barred by limitation and cannot be revived by permitting late payment. The judgment cites no specific statutory provision or earlier case for this conclusion.

rule.if: civil_appeal_concerns_counterclaim and counterclaim_claimed_for_improvements and counterclaim_issue_unframed and court_fee_unpaid_within_deadline and payment_sought_after_deadline

predicates.civil_appeal_concerns_counterclaim: The proceeding is an appeal in which a party challenges the treatment of a counterclaim.
predicates.counterclaim_claimed_for_improvements: A party claimed a counterclaim for improvements made to property.
predicates.counterclaim_issue_unframed: The trial court did not frame an issue concerning the counterclaim.
predicates.court_fee_unpaid_within_deadline: The party did not pay the court fee on the counterclaim within the prescribed time.
predicates.payment_sought_after_deadline: The party sought permission to pay the court fee after the prescribed time had expired.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a counterclaim for improvements that was not made an issue and its court fee was unpaid by the deadline, a request to pay after the deadline is not permitted.

issues.legal_issue: A receiving court may continue a suit from the stage reached before the plaint was returned when evidence has already been adduced.
material_facts: A plaint was returned for presentation to a court with the proper pecuniary jurisdiction after an amendment seeking damages for use and occupation made the suit exceed the trial court's jurisdiction.
Evidence had already been adduced by the parties.
The High Court directed the receiving court to proceed from the stage at which the suit had been transferred to it.
issues.conclusion: The direction to proceed from the stage at which the suit had been transferred was not illegal and did not warrant interference.
issues.legal_principle: Ordinarily, when a plaint is returned for presentation to the proper court, the matter may have to start from the beginning. Where evidence has already been adduced, however, the receiving court may proceed from the stage reached. The judgment cites no specific statutory provision or earlier case for this procedural principle.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_continuation_after_plaint_return and plaint_returned_for_proper_court and evidence_already_adduced and continuation_from_prior_stage_directed

predicates.appeal_challenges_continuation_after_pla: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a direction about how a suit should continue after its plaint was returned.
predicates.plaint_returned_for_proper_court: A plaint was returned for presentation to a court with proper jurisdiction.
predicates.evidence_already_adduced: The parties had already adduced evidence before the plaint was returned.
predicates.continuation_from_prior_stage_directed: The receiving court was directed to continue the suit from the stage it had reached before the return.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges continuation of a suit after its plaint was returned, and evidence had already been adduced before a direction to continue from the prior stage, the receiving court may continue from that stage.
